matches.rationale: Both identify that the Abstract claims FID range 2.38–2.64 (or 2.15–2.38 in pred_id 3) but this misrepresents the actual results in Table 4, which shows higher FID values at certain replacement ratios. The ground truth notes cherry-picking favorable results; pred_id 3 identifies the Abstract's FID range is inconsistent with body text reporting 2.38–2.64.

Ground truth concerns ambiguity in Equation 2's regression objective definition and the conditioning variable c. No finding addresses the formal definition of L_reg or the ambiguity about conditioning in the distillation objective.

Ground truth identifies missing hyperparameter details in Table C.1 (gradient clipping specification, warmup schedule details, batch size clarification). No finding addresses these specific protocol omissions in the appendix table.

Both identify overstated claims about grafting's general utility. Ground truth notes the Introduction's absolute language ('proves,' 'demonstrates') overstates limited experimental scope. Pred_id 4 identifies the Abstract's claim that grafting 'consistently outperforms... across all replacement ratios' contradicts the 100% replacement failure, showing overgeneralization.

Ground truth concerns Table 4's selective omission of actual FID values (using '✗' for FID > 50) and ambiguity in ΔFLOPs columns. No finding addresses the missing FID values or the confusion between ΔFLOPs_op and ΔFLOPs_ft columns.

Ground truth identifies fabricated relevance of reference [4] (plant grafting paper) to the computational method. No finding addresses this specific reference misattribution or the false interdisciplinary grounding claim.

Both identify inconsistency in the locality analysis claims. Ground truth notes the problematic interpretation of L_k > 0.5 and lack of variance reporting. Pred_id 2 identifies direct contradiction between text claiming 'all 28 layers exhibit L_k > 0.7, with 22 layers exceeding 0.85' versus Figure 2 caption stating 'only 15 out of 28 layers exhibit values exceeding 0.5.'

Ground truth concerns missing experimental protocol details for PixArt-Σ evaluation (sampling steps comparison, LoRA vs full finetuning). No finding addresses whether baseline and grafted models used the same evaluation protocol or finetuning method.

Both identify misleading comparison claims. Ground truth notes the grafted depth-to-width model (712M params, FID 2.77) is compared unfairly to TinyDiT-D14 (340M params) without acknowledging the 2× parameter difference. Pred_id 1 identifies the claim that FID 2.77 'surpasses' the baseline FID 2.27, which is a direct contradiction since lower FID is better.

Ground truth identifies omission of limitations and failure cases from the Conclusion (100% replacement failure, PixArt-Σ artifacts, bias risks). No finding specifically addresses the Conclusion's failure to acknowledge these limitations.

Both identify issues with the PixArt-Σ speedup claim. Ground truth notes Table 5 reports speedup at non-standard batch size=2 without justification or reporting at other batch sizes. Pred_id 6 identifies that the claimed 1.43× speedup does not match any value in Table 5 (which shows 1.59× and 1.21×).

Both identify that the Abstract's FID claims mix results from different data percentages. Ground truth notes the best results use 20% data (not 10%) but the Abstract claims '<2% compute' based on 10% data. Pred_id 7 identifies Figure 1(c) mixes 20%-data and 10%-data results without disclosure, inconsistent with Table 4.

Ground truth concerns inappropriate promotional language ('revolutionary,' 'paradigm shift,' 'unprecedented') in the Introduction. No finding addresses rhetorical manipulation or marketing-style language in the paper.

Ground truth identifies incorrect FLOP calculation formula in Section H.1 and inconsistency with reported ΔFLOPs_op reductions in Table 4. No finding addresses the mathematical correctness of FLOP formulas or their consistency with reported percentage reductions.

Ground truth identifies misrepresentation of reference [52] (progressive network grafting paper) as relevant prior work on architectural editing for generative models. No finding addresses this specific reference misattribution in the Related Work section.
